MAJOR ARCANA

Death — Meaning

Major Arcana

  • CategoryMajor Arcana
  • SymbolScorpio / Number 13
  • UprightAn ending, Change, A new beginning
  • ReversedCannot let go, Fear of change, Putting it off

A card about finishing one thing so that something new can begin.

Death stands for "An ending, Change, A new beginning" when upright, and "Cannot let go, Fear of change, Putting it off" when reversed. Consider drawing a line under a habit or method that no longer fits. Ending something can free up time and energy for what comes next.

Reading it in a decision — In a situation of ending something, like leaving a job, read this card as turning your eyes first to the time and energy an ending creates, rather than to your reasons for continuing. Reversed, do not try to end everything at once — start with a small ending.

The decision this speaks to: When you're torn about leaving your job

SYMBOLS

The symbols in the picture

A skeletal knight on a white horse, and a sunrise in the distance. It stands for an ending, and the beginning that comes after. This card does not predict anyone's death.

UPRIGHT

Upright meaning

  • An ending
  • Change
  • A new beginning

Consider drawing a line under a habit or method that no longer fits. Ending something can free up time and energy for what comes next.

Ease of moving forward3 / 5 (Depends on the conditions)

What you may not be noticing
Is there something that no longer fits who you are now?
What to watch out for
When you change things, allow time for yourself and others to adjust.
What do you really want?
What would feel lighter if you drew a line under it?
A thought you can let go of
You do not have to keep a habit whose role is finished.
A hint for choosing
Which option makes the next step easier to picture after the ending?

REVERSED

Reversed meaning

  • Cannot let go
  • Fear of change
  • Putting it off

You may feel both the wish to end something and the fear of changing. Instead of changing everything at once, think about a small ending first.

Ease of moving forward2 / 5 (Prepare and rethink first)

What you may not be noticing
Are you stretching things out because ending them is frightening?
What to watch out for
Separate what makes you resist change from the preparation you need.
What do you really want?
What are you afraid you would lose if things changed?
A thought you can let go of
You do not have to keep going just because you have continued this far.
A hint for choosing
Which option lets you start with a small ending?

FOR YOUR DECISION

Hints for your decision

How to read it when you are deciding

Death is often thought an ominous card, but its essence is 'endings and rebirth.' On the banner of the skeleton on the white horse, white roses are drawn, showing that beyond an ending lies a new beginning. In a decision, it gives you the courage to draw a line under a matter you are torn between continuing and ending. Thinking about what you would use the time and room an ending creates for makes the judgment easier.

How to face a familiar worry

This card often appears when you are torn about letting go of work, a relationship, or a habit you have continued for a long time. Upright, it is time to thank what has finished its role and draw the line. Reversed, you may be piling up postponements out of fear of change. Be aware that not deciding an ending is itself a choice.

Questions to ask yourself before you decide

Is there something that should end, which you still hold onto with regret? Can you accept something ending as preparation for the next beginning? If you kept refusing change, what would you look like in a year? In what order will you let things go?

"Ease of moving forward" is the strength of the tailwind behind an option if you move on it now — not a judgment of whether things will turn out well or badly.

Now that you have read the meaning, turn to the decision in front of you. Draw a card and lay your two options side by side.
